references.text: God promises that Israel will be His treasured possession and a kingdom of priests if they obey His voice and keep His covenant, with conditions similar to those in Deut. 28:1.
The blessings that follow from walking in God's laws and keeping His commandments, paralleling the promise in Deut. 28:1.
The condition of listening carefully to the Lord's voice and keeping all His commands is repeated here with a promise of blessing.
God promises to set Israel high above all nations, the same promise given in Deut. 28:1.
It expands on the promise that Israel will be the head and not the tail, above and not beneath, through obedience to God's commands.
Samuel emphasizes that obedience is better than sacrifice, and that listening to the Lord's voice is crucial.
Jeremiah quotes God's command to listen to His voice, with the promise that He will be their God.
Zechariah prophesies blessing for those who carefully listen to the Lord's voice.
Peter describes believers as a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, reflecting the promise made to Israel.
Blessing is promised to those who hear and keep what is written, similar to the condition of obedience in Deut. 28:1.
